description: Whitewashed stone gone patchy closes both sides under a corrugated tin roof with the rafters showing; hurdle pens tied with baler twine, straw trodden into hollows, a green enamel kettle on a shelf beside two mugs.

Tarred feather-edge boarding down both sides under a beam ceiling with bales stacked up into it; a galvanised bucket gone chalky hanging by its handle from a nail, straw ankle-deep around the hurdle pens.

Breeze-block to waist height and boards above, a corrugated tin roof closing overhead; a pitchfork stood against the far boards, straw pulled apart from a cut bale, two lambs tucked tight against a broad cream-fleeced ewe.

Whitewashed stone walls gone butter-yellow with age closing both sides, a beam roof overhead; a halter looped over the top hurdle rail, a coiled rope on a nail, straw trodden into warm hollows underfoot.

Corrugated tin on a timber frame with the rafters showing overhead and tarred boards down both sides; a lamp hanging on its hooked flex, its light landing on the plank walkway and the damp curls of a lamb pressed against the ewe's flank.

Whitewashed stone gone patchy on both sides, a corrugated tin roof closing it overhead; the open doorway with its own timber jamb frames the field small and hazy beyond, that outside light coming back in across the straw by the threshold and the nearest hurdle rail.

Feather-edge boarding silvered by age down both sides under a beam ceiling; a wooden chair with a coat over its back stands at the pen end, straw bales stacked up into the rafters, two lambs no taller than the hurdle's bottom rail nuzzling the ewe's chest.

Breeze-block walls to waist height with boards above them and a corrugated tin roof overhead; a folded heap of clean sacks on a shelf, a besom broom stood in the corner, baler twine holding every hurdle joint.

Tarred feather-edge boarding on both sides, a beam ceiling with bales stacked up into it above; the doorway's own timber sill low and worn, the field beyond it hazy and small, its light landing on the ewe's back just inside the pen.

Corrugated tin roof on a timber frame closing overhead, whitewashed stone walls gone patchy on both sides; a red plastic feed scoop leaning against the hurdle rail, straw pulled apart from a cut bale half-spread across the pen floor.

Whitewashed stone on both sides under a corrugated tin roof with the rafters showing; a lamp on its hooked flex hangs in plain sight, its light falling on the plank walkway, a hay rack wired to the hurdle, straw ankle-deep below it.

Tarred boarding down both sides, a beam ceiling closing overhead; the low window in the near wall with its own timber sill frames a blurred hedge beyond, that diffused light coming back onto the straw and the two lambs pressed to the ewe's side.

Feather-edge boarding silvered by age on both sides under corrugated tin closing overhead; a leaning stack of spare hurdles against the far wall, a galvanised bucket brimming beside the pen, baler twine looped at every joint.

A dry stone wall with moss thick on its north side, last year's grass bleached fawn with new green threading up through it; a ring feeder with hay pulled out loose around it, a water trough brimming over at one corner.

A hawthorn hedge with the first buds only just breaking, a gap in the stone wall shut with a single hurdle; a galvanised trough against the wall, a loose mob of ewes spread across the field, two lambs close at one ewe's flank.

Bare-branched ash along the far boundary, last year's grass still bleached fawn; a faded blue gate on a rope hinge, its iron strap hinges worn silver-bright at the post, a ring feeder with hay scattered on the mud around it.

Dead bracken flattened along the foot of the stone wall, a mud-slick churned gateway; a water trough brimming, a field gate on a rope hinge painted a chalky cream, ewes spread unevenly across the near half of the field.

Rushes standing dead and pale in the wet corner, last year's grass bleached fawn; a ring feeder with hay pulled out round it, two lambs no higher than the ewe's knee working around her hind legs, a stone wall closing the far side.

A bare thorn hedge with the first buds only just breaking, a frost-stiff tussock at the wall's foot; a galvanised bucket hanging by its handle from the gate post, a water trough along the wall, ewes grazing in a loose uneven spread.

Dead bracken flattened along the stone wall, a puddle standing in the gateway; a ring feeder with hay pulled loose around its base, a faded blue gate on a rope hinge, two lambs pressing against the ewe's flank.

Bare-branched ash along the boundary, last year's grass bleached fawn with green coming up through it; a gap in the stone wall shut with a hurdle, a water trough brimming at one corner, molehills scattered across the near ground.

Rushes standing dead and pale in the wet corner, moss thick on the north side of the stone wall; a faded blue gate on a rope hinge, a ring feeder, a loose mob of ewes spread unevenly across the field with one ewe set apart near the trough.

A hawthorn hedge just breaking bud at the field's top end, a mud-slick churned gateway below it; a coiled rope on the gate post, a galvanised trough along the wall, two lambs no taller than the ewe's chest nosing the hay scattered round the feeder.

Last year's grass still bleached fawn with new green threading up, a frost-stiff tussock at the wall's base; a ring feeder with hay pulled out round it, a water trough brimming over, molehills dotting the uneven ground.

Dead bracken flattened along the foot of the thorn hedge, bare branches still showing above it; a faded blue gate on a rope hinge, its iron latch worn silver-bright, a ring feeder, ewes in a loose uneven group with one standing apart by the wall.
